The authors state they integrate the sdmetrics library to provide standardized privacy-utility evaluation across methods, while also noting that SDV's sdmetrics framework is not directly applicable to the high dimensionality of ICD codes, prompting supplementary custom metrics. SDV's sdmetrics package is cited and partially integrated as one component of the paper's evaluation suite, run alongside bespoke discriminative and prevalence metrics rather than as the sole benchmarking tool.
evidence: "Addressing the fragmentation of assessment metrics in the field, we integrate the sdmetrics library to establish a rigorous evaluation suite" -- though elsewhere the paper notes "modern standardized frameworks like SDV's sdmetrics ... are not applicable due to the high dimensionality of ICD codes."
venue: Machine Learning for Healthcare (preprint, under review)
needs: The paper contains a contradiction: it claims to integrate sdmetrics for its evaluation suite in the contributions list, yet elsewhere states sdmetrics is not applicable to high-dimensional ICD codes. Unclear how much of the final evaluation actually runs sdmetrics versus custom metrics built instead of it.

title: Actionability of Synthetic Data in a Heterogeneous and Rare Healthcare Demographic; Adolescents and Young Adults (AYAs) with Cancer
summary: A population-based cohort study of 3735 adolescents and young adults with cancer that tests how sample size affects the 'actionability' (veracity, utility, and privacy concealment) of synthetic data generated at varying training and output sizes. The authors train four generator architectures — FastML, Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, and a DP-CGAN built atop SDV modules — on shrinking subsamples and evaluate the resulting synthetic datasets with prdc coverage/density metrics and SDMetrics' CAP algorithm for privacy risk. SDV's FastML and Gaussian Copula synthesizers, and its CTGAN implementation, are run directly as the study's evaluation generators, with SDMetrics supplying the attribute-inference privacy score.
affiliations: Netherlands Cancer Institute; Erasmus University Medical Centre
Netherlands Cancer Institute; Erasmus University Medical Centre
evidence: "We tested four SD generator architectures from the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) Python library... The first was a speed-optimised Gaussian copula generator (hereafter 'Fast ML') and the other was a classical Gaussian copula generator... a Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN)..."
needs: DP-CGAN is described as 'built on top of existing SDV-library modules' but is not itself an official SDV synthesizer; not counted as a distinct SDV component.

title: Adaptive and Robust Watermark for Generative Tabular Data
summary: This paper proposes a theoretically grounded watermarking algorithm for generative tabular data, providing guarantees on fidelity, detectability, robustness, and hardness of decoding, and validating them on synthetic and real-world tabular datasets. To produce the synthetic data used in its experiments, the authors generate tables with CTGAN, TVAE, and Gaussian Copula using the default hyperparameters found in the SDV library, and measure downstream machine-learning efficacy (MLE gap) as a fidelity/utility metric. SDV's CTGAN, TVAE, and GaussianCopula synthesizers are run directly via the library as the data-generation backbone underlying the paper's watermarking experiments.
evidence: "For synthetic data generation using three generative methods mentioned in the paper, we follow the default hyperparameters found in the SDV library [Patki et al., 2016]." CTGAN, TVAE, and Gaussian Copula outputs are then evaluated via MLE gap and used throughout the watermarking experiments.

title: Advancing Cardiovascular Disease Diagnosis: A Robust ML Ecosystem Integrating Early Detection, Responsible AI Framework, and Causal Inference
summary: This preprint develops a machine learning ecosystem for cardiovascular disease diagnosis, combining tabular neural networks (TabNet, TabPFN, FT-Transformer) and ensemble models with interpretability (SHAP, counterfactuals), fairness auditing, uncertainty quantification, and causal inference to build a responsible AI framework validated on multi-regional heart disease datasets. The authors use CTGAN to generate synthetic instances that equalize disease frequency across sex subgroups for bias mitigation, and separately use the Gaussian Copula method to simulate a high-data augmentation scenario, ultimately finding both synthetic augmentation approaches degrade discriminative performance relative to real data. CTGAN's conditional generator and mode-specific normalization, and SDV's Gaussian Copula synthesizer, are both run as data augmentation methods within the empirical pipeline, evaluated as one of several techniques and found to have limitations.
evidence: "We created several synthetic instances from the combined dataset using Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN)... [CTGAN] uses mode-specific normalization via Variational Gaussian Mixture Models (VGM)..." and separately "we simulated a high-data environment by augmenting the dataset using the Gaussian Copula method."

title: Advancing Retail Data Science: Comprehensive Evaluation of Synthetic Data
summary: This paper proposes an evaluation framework for synthetic retail data along three axes -- fidelity, utility, and privacy -- applied to five generative models trained on a retail basket dataset (Complete Journey). It distinguishes stability from generalizability for fidelity, tests downstream classification utility, and uses differential-privacy-style distance metrics for privacy. CTGAN is run as one of five tabular generative models benchmarked across all three evaluation axes, with its mode-specific normalization discussed as a mechanism for handling imbalanced categorical distributions.
evidence: "We examined 5 generative models to produce the synthetic datasets: GAN-based tabular generative models ((1) CTGAN[50], (2) AutoGAN)...models are cloned from the cited repositories" -- CTGAN evaluated across fidelity, utility, and privacy metrics alongside four other generators.

title: Adversarial Causal Tuning for Realistic Time-series Generation
summary: This paper introduces Adversarial Causal Tuning (ACT), a methodology for causal-model tuning that searches over causal discovery pipelines and adversarial discriminators to select the causal model best matching a real time-series dataset, enabling realistic simulation, what-if scenario generation, and causal benchmark creation. It is evaluated on real, semi-synthetic, and synthetic time-series datasets against non-causal generative baselines. In these experiments, SDV's CPAR (sequential PAR model) is run as one of several comparison baselines alongside CausalTime and TimeVAE.
evidence: "We compare against the authors' implementation of CausalTime, CPAR as implemented by SDV (Patki et al., 2016), and TimeVAE (Desai et al., 2021) available through the Synthcity framework."

title: Adversarially-learned Inference via an Ensemble of Discrete Undirected Graphical Models
summary: This paper proposes an adversarially-trained ensemble of discrete undirected graphical models (AGMs) that generalizes across inference tasks without retraining, evaluated on MNIST and Caltech-101 for both generation and inference quality. The CTGAN paper (Xu et al. 2019) appears only in the reference list, with no engagement in the body text describing use of CTGAN's methods or model. CTGAN is cited only, never run or discussed in the body.
evidence: CTGAN citation (Xu et al. 2019) appears only in the bibliography list; no body passage discusses or uses it.

title: AgentCTG: Harnessing Multi-Agent Collaboration for Fine-Grained Precise Control in Text Generation
summary: This paper proposes AgentCTG, a multi-agent LLM framework for fine-grained controlled text generation, introducing agent collaboration, auto-prompting, and reflection mechanisms, and demonstrates it on tasks including toxicity mitigation, sentiment transformation, and a new Character-Driven Rewriting task for online navigation role-play. The work is about controlled natural-language generation with LLM agents and has no discernible connection to tabular synthetic data. The metadata lists a citation to the CTGAN paper, but no SDV-family mention appears anywhere in the extracted full text, suggesting a mis-attributed or lost citation rather than any actual use of CTGAN.
evidence: No SDV-family term appears anywhere in the full text despite the metadata listing a citation to the CTGAN paper; the work concerns LLM-based controlled text generation with no relation to tabular synthetic data.
needs: The citation to ctgan-neurips-2019 in the metadata cannot be located in the full text; this is likely a mis-attributed or lost reference and the entry may not belong in the index at all.

title: AIGT: AI Generative Table Based on Prompt
summary: This paper proposes AIGT, a prompt-enhanced, LLM-based framework for synthesizing tabular data that leverages table metadata (descriptions and schemas) as prompts and uses long-token partitioning to scale to wide tables, evaluated on 20 public datasets plus two Alipay risk-control datasets. CTGAN and TVAE are run as two of five state-of-the-art baseline synthesizers, trained for 300 epochs, and compared against AIGT on machine-learning-efficacy and data-quality metrics across many datasets. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE models are used as comparison baselines against which the proposed LLM-based generator is benchmarked, while a Gaussian copula model from the SDV paper is cited only descriptively as prior work.
evidence: "We evaluate AIGT along-side five other SOTA tabular data synthesis algorithms: CTGAN, TVAE, TabDDPM, GReaT and TapTap... For CTGAN and TVAE, we set the training epochs to 300, except for those datasets that have less than 5k data."
needs: Unclear whether CTGAN/TVAE were run via the sdv-dev package or an independent reimplementation; hyperparameter table shows only epoch counts, not sdv-specific constructor arguments, though training/sampling time table treats them as distinct runnable baselines.

title: Airline Passenger Name Record Generation using Generative Adversarial Networks
summary: This work proposes a GAN-based method (Cramér GAN with categorical feature embedding and a Cross-Net architecture) to generate realistic synthetic Passenger Name Records for airlines, addressing data-sharing and privacy constraints in the travel industry, and evaluates it on a real PNR dataset for distribution matching, memorization, and downstream predictive tasks. For encoding numerical features, the authors adopt the Gaussian-sampling discretization technique proposed by Patki et al. (2016), the Synthetic Data Vault paper, implementing it in their own pipeline rather than running SDV's software.
evidence: To convert a discrete value to a numerical one, we replace it with a value sampled from a Gaussian distribution centered at the midpoint of [ac,bc] and with σ = (b−a)/6 as proposed in (Patki et al., 2016).
venue: ICML 2018 Workshop on Theoretical Foundations and Applications of Deep Generative Models

title: An algorithm for drug discovery based on deep learning with an example of developing a drug for the treatment of lung cancer
summary: This preprint presents a multi-stage deep-learning pipeline for drug discovery, covering target identification via gene-expression analysis, prediction of drug-protein interactions, and IC50 prediction for candidate inhibitors, applied to an example of lung cancer therapy. To augment the patient gene-expression dataset used for target gene selection, the authors generate 50,000 synthetic patient records. The sdv library's CTGAN module is run as the generator producing this synthetic patient data that feeds the downstream feature-selection analysis.
evidence: "To implement GAN, we used the sdv library (5), in particular, the CTGAN module (6)." They generated 50k patients' data used for downstream feature selection with Lasso regression.
needs: Only the abstract/body snippet around the citation was available in full; broader context of how the 50k synthetic records were validated is not detailed.

title: Amalgam: Hybrid LLM-PGM Synthesis Algorithm for Accuracy and Realism
summary: This preprint introduces Amalgam, a hybrid data-synthesis algorithm that combines a Probabilistic Graphical Model with an LLM, using PGM-derived summary statistics to condition zero-shot LLM sample generation for synthetic tabular/relational data with privacy and realism guarantees. The paper frames its contribution against two prior approaches, PGMs and Deep Learning models, citing CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) as an example of the latter category whose resulting data 'tends to capture a less accurate distribution.' CTGAN is only cited as prior deep-learning-based synthesis work, not run or benchmarked in the experiments.
evidence: "Deep Learning models (Jordon et al., 2018; Guo et al., 2023; Xu et al., 2019)... the resulting data tends to capture a less accurate distribution (Tao et al., 2021)" -- CTGAN cited as representative deep-learning synthesis approach the paper positions itself against.

title: An Analysis of the Deployment of Models Trained on Private Tabular Synthetic Data: Unexpected Surprises
summary: This paper studies how differentially private synthetic tabular data generation affects both model utility and algorithmic fairness, and shows that model performance evaluated on synthetic data can misestimate real-world deployment performance. The authors run three DP synthesizers (PrivBayes, QUAIL+PATECTGAN, QUAIL+DPCTGAN) on the Adult and COMPAS datasets and measure utility/fairness gaps between evaluation and deployment. CTGAN, as introduced by Xu et al. (2019), underlies two of the three synthesizers evaluated, combined with PATE and DP-SGD mechanisms as the conditional generator producing the differentially private synthetic training data.
evidence: "Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN) (Xu et al., 2019) is an approach for generating tabular data... CTGAN can provide differential privacy by applying the PATE framework. We call this combination PATE-CTGAN... which is similar to PATE-GAN"; two of the three evaluated synthesizers (QUAIL+PATECTGAN, QUAIL+DPCTGAN) are CTGAN-based.
needs: Unclear whether the CTGAN/DP variants (PATE-CTGAN, DPCTGAN) were run via the sdv-dev CTGAN package or an external implementation (e.g., smartnoise-sdk per Rosenblatt et al. 2020); treated as api_user of existing packaged synthesizers.

title: AnoGAN for Tabular Data: A Novel Approach to Anomaly Detection
summary: This preprint adapts the AnoGAN anomaly-detection framework, originally developed for images, to tabular data by first synthesizing samples with CTGAN and then applying AnoGAN's reconstruction-error scoring to distinguish anomalies from normal points. The authors identify prediction randomness in CTGAN's outputs, traced to the Gumbel Softmax activation used for categorical columns, and replace it with a 'hard' Gumbel Softmax variant to make generation more deterministic before running AnoGAN on the resulting synthetic data. CTGAN's generator architecture and its Gumbel-softmax-based categorical sampling mechanism are directly modified, and the modified generator supplies the synthetic samples underlying the entire empirical evaluation.
evidence: "In our research methodology, the utilization of the original CT-GAN ... implementation plays a pivotal role in generating synthetic samples for anomaly detection... we mitigate this randomness through the implementation of a hard Gumbel Softmax approach" -- CTGAN's generator is directly modified and its output drives the whole experiment.

title: Artificial Intelligence for In Silico Clinical Trials: A Review
summary: This review surveys AI and machine learning methods applied to in silico clinical trials, covering clinical simulation, individualized predictive modeling, and computer-aided trial design, with an emphasis on ML problem formulations and data sources for each task. It does not run any generative models itself but cites relevant prior work as part of its broad literature synthesis. CTGAN is cited in the reference list as an example of conditional GAN modeling of tabular data, with no experiment or engagement in the body text.
affiliations: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; Carle Illinois College of Medicine
evidence: Reference [21] cited as 'Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks' corresponding to 'Lei Xu, Maria Skoularidou, Alfredo Cuesta-Infante, and Kalyan Veeramachaneni. Modeling tabular data using conditional gan.' with no in-body discussion found beyond the citation marker.
needs: Full body context around citation [21] was not retrieved; only the reference list entry and a citation marker location were available, so engagement depth beyond a passing mention could not be verified.

title: Assessing Deep Generative Models on Time-Series Network Data
summary: This preprint evaluates three recent GAN architectures for generating synthetic network load (time-series telecom traffic) data, testing whether models trained on the synthetic data can substitute for real data in downstream forecasting tasks, using the Telecom Italia dataset and a mix of qualitative and quantitative metrics. CTGAN is cited as one of the SDV-family papers referenced for one of the three evaluated GAN architectures. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization approach is one of the generative methods run as an evaluation subject alongside the other GAN architectures compared.
evidence: Cites ctgan-neurips-2019 while evaluating 'three recent GAN architectures' on network load data, per the abstract's framing of comparative GAN benchmarking for time-series network traffic.
needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev package, reimplemented, or merely one of the cited architectures. Cannot verify which two other GAN architectures were tested or whether CTGAN's results were prominent.

title: Assessing Generative Models for Structured Data
summary: This preprint proposes new statistical methods for directly assessing synthetic tabular data quality by examining inter-column dependencies (marginal, pairwise, and higher-order joint cumulants) rather than relying on train-synthetic-test-real utility metrics. Applying these methods to GPT-2 (few-shot and fine-tuned) and a GAN baseline across Adult, Breast Cancer, and Credit datasets, the authors find that none of the generative methods reproduce the real data's higher-order dependency structure. CTGAN, run via its implementation from the Synthetic Data Vault, serves as the GAN baseline compared against the LLM-based approaches throughout the empirical evaluation.
affiliations: University of Texas at El Paso
Pacific Northwest National Laboratory; University of Texas at El Paso
evidence: "we used the CTGAN 35 implementation from Synthetic Data Vault. 23 CTGAN is a method used to fine-tune GANs to generate realistic synthetic tabular data."

title: AugMask: Training Diffusion Models on Incomplete Tabular Data via Stochastic Augmentation and Masking
summary: This paper proposes AugMask, a plug-and-play training framework that adapts missing-unaware diffusion backbones to incomplete tabular data by using stochastic augmentation to fill missing values as uncertain conditioning context while masking the denoising loss to only originally observed coordinates. The method is evaluated across many datasets and missingness regimes, showing that standard diffusion generators enhanced with AugMask outperform specialized missing-aware baselines. CTGAN is one of several missing-unaware generator baselines run in the experiments, explicitly using the Synthetic Data Vault's CTGAN implementation, and is also enhanced with the authors' augmentation strategy for comparison.
evidence: "CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019): We follow the popular implementation in the Synthetic Data Vault package (see https://github.com/sdv-dev/CTGAN)."

title: Data Augmentation with GAN increases the Performance of Arrhythmia Classification for an Unbalanced Dataset
summary: This conference paper trains a GAN to generate synthetic ECG signals from the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database to augment an unbalanced dataset, using the synthetic data to train a classifier that is then tested on real ECG data, showing improved classification performance. CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) is mentioned only once in passing as an example of GAN-based tabular data synthesis, and does not appear anywhere else in the text; it is a bibliography-only citation, not something run in the study.
evidence: With GAN, audio files can be synthesized (Donahue et al., 2018), as well as tabular data (Xu et al., 2019). No further mention of CTGAN appears in the body text; it is confirmed to be a bibliographic citation only.
venue: 4th International Eurasian Conference on Science, Engineering and Technology (EurasianSciEnTech 2022)

title: Data Augmentation for Imbalanced Regression
summary: This paper addresses imbalanced continuous or discrete covariates in regression, proposing a two-step algorithm combining weighted resampling with data augmentation to explore a wider covariate support before re-weighting toward a target distribution. Six data-generation approaches are compared numerically, including copula, GAN, random forest, and interpolation methods, with an actuarial application illustrating the approach. Two of these six generators -- Gaussian Copula and a Conditional GAN -- are explicitly run 'using the python-package Synthetic Data Vault', making SDV's GaussianCopula and CTGAN synthesizers evaluation subjects alongside SynthPop, SMOTE, and mixture-model approaches.
evidence: "Copula: Gaussian Copula Model, using the python-package Synthetic Data Vault • GAN: Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks, using the python-package Synthetic Data Vault"

title: An Augmented Surprise-guided Sequential Learning Framework for Predicting the Melt Pool Geometry
summary: This preprint proposes SurpriseAF-BO, a surprise-guided sequential Bayesian optimization framework for predicting melt pool depth, width, and length in metal additive manufacturing from limited process data. The authors then extend it into CT-SurpriseAF-BO by augmenting the small training set with synthetic samples, improving prediction RMSE without additional physical experiments. CTGAN is run as the synthetic data generator underpinning this augmentation, with a reported hyperparameter table (embedding dim, generator dim, discriminator dim, generator/discriminator lr) matching the sdv-dev CTGAN implementation.
affiliations: University of Texas at San Antonio
evidence: Table 8 lists CTGAN hyperparameters 'embedding dim', 'generator dim', 'discriminator dim', 'generator lr', 'discriminator lr' with selected values, matching the sdv-dev CTGAN constructor signature, and the paper reports RMSE improvements of up to 20.85% from CTGAN-augmented synthetic samples in the CT-SurpriseAF-BO framework.

title: Augmenting Offline Reinforcement Learning with State-only Interactions
summary: This preprint proposes DITS, a method that augments offline reinforcement learning by using state-only online interactions: a conditional diffusion model generates high-return trajectories which are then stitched to the original offline data to improve downstream RL. It evaluates the fidelity of generated versus expert data distributions using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic and Pearson rank correlation, metrics it attributes to Patki et al. (2016), the original Synthetic Data Vault paper. SDV is cited only as the source of these evaluation metrics, not run as a synthesizer or library in the pipeline.
evidence: "The metrics included the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic and the Pearson rank correlation (Patki et al., 2016)."
needs: SDV is cited only for a metric methodology, not run as software; no sdmetrics library invocation is described.

title: AutoDiff: combining Auto-encoder and Diffusion model for tabular data synthesizing
summary: This paper proposes AutoDiff, a tabular data synthesizer that combines an autoencoder for handling heterogeneous features with a diffusion model in the resulting latent space, aiming to improve statistical fidelity and downstream ML utility over prior GAN- and diffusion-based synthesizers. The authors benchmark AutoDiff against CTGAN, TVAE, CTABGAN+, Stasy, and TabDDPM across 15 public tabular datasets on fidelity, ML efficacy, and privacy metrics. CTGAN and TVAE, both citing the SDV-family CTGAN paper, are run as baseline synthesizers among several comparison models, not modified or extended.
evidence: "Numerical comparisons of AutoDiff with other models (with publicly available codes), namely, CTGAN [24], TVAE [24], CTABGAN+ [26], Stasy [11], and TabDDPM [13] are conducted comprehensively across 15 real-world datasets under various metrics."

title: Automated Privacy-Preserving Techniques via Meta-Learning
summary: This paper proposes AUTOPRIV, a meta-learning framework that automates privacy-preserving data configuration by predicting the predictive performance and privacy risk of a large set of privacy-preservation techniques, removing the need for manual expert tuning. It evaluates six synthesis/protection methods, including deep-learning generators, differentially-private GANs, and an interpolation-based approach, across multiple hyperparameter optimisation strategies. SDV's CopulaGAN, TVAE, and CTGAN are run directly from the SDV library as three of the six generation methods whose predictive performance and privacy risk are evaluated and compared.
evidence: "We use general deep learning-based models from the SDV library [46], namely Copula GAN, TVAE, and CTGAN."

title: Autoregressive Synthesis of Sparse and Semi-Structured Mixed-Type Data
summary: This paper presents ORiGAMi, an autoregressive transformer that synthesizes semi-structured JSON records directly by tokenizing key/value/structural tokens and encoding tree-path positions, avoiding the flattening required by tabular synthesizers. It is evaluated against VAE, GAN, diffusion, and autoregressive baselines across six datasets on fidelity, utility, detection, and privacy metrics, outperforming them in 17 of 18 comparisons. TVAE and CTGAN are run using the SDV library's implementation as two of the six baselines, and SDMetrics-based scores (extended by the authors for structural missingness) underlie the fidelity/utility/detection evaluation framework.
evidence: "We use the SDV [24] library implementation with default hyperparameters (300 epochs) for both models" (TVAE and CTGAN), and standard tabular evaluation metrics via SDMetrics are extended for the paper's fidelity/utility/detection scoring.

title: Balanced Mixed-Type Tabular Data Synthesis with Diffusion Models
summary: This paper introduces a fairness-aware tabular diffusion model that incorporates sensitive-attribute guidance to generate balanced synthetic data with improved demographic parity and equalized odds compared to prior tabular synthesis methods. It evaluates its diffusion-based generator against several baselines including GAN- and VAE-based tabular synthesizers on datasets such as Adult, Bank, and COMPAS. CTGAN and TVAE, described as GAN- and VAE-based tabular synthesis approaches with 'user-friendly implementation' credited to the SDV paper (Patki et al., 2016), are run as two of several comparison baselines that the proposed method is reported to generally outperform.
evidence: "It generally outperforms CTGAN and TVAE." CTGAN and TVAE are listed as baseline methods described with 'user-friendly implementation in (Patki et al., 2016)', i.e. the SDV library, and compared against the proposed diffusion model.
needs: Full results table containing the CTGAN/TVAE comparison was not shown in the excerpted text, so exact metric values and whether SDV's own CTGAN/TVAE code (vs. the original authors' implementations) was used could not be directly confirmed.

title: Balancing Optimality and Diversity: Human-Centered Decision Making through Generative Curation
summary: This paper proposes generative curation, a decision-theoretic framework for algorithms that produce a diverse portfolio of quantitatively strong recommendations for a human decision-maker to choose from, formalizing a trade-off between optimality and qualitative diversity via a Gaussian-process model. It develops neural generative and sequential optimization implementations and validates them on synthetic experiments and a police redistricting case study. CTGAN is cited only in passing, in the introduction's list of areas where generative models have been applied (synthetic data generation), with no use of the SDV library or its methods in the work itself.
evidence: "models have been successfully applied in areas ranging from design optimization ..., synthetic data generation (Xu et al. 2019), to black-box optimization..." is the only mention of the CTGAN paper, in the introduction's literature survey; no CTGAN code or method is used.

title: Balancing thermal comfort datasets: We GAN, but should we?
summary: This paper investigates class-balancing techniques for imbalanced thermal-comfort survey datasets and proposes comfortGAN, a modified conditional GAN, comparing it against SMOTE, ADASYN, TGAN, and CTGAN across three public thermal comfort datasets. The results show comfortGAN generally improves downstream classification accuracy more than the other augmentation methods, though gains shrink when classes are merged. TGAN and CTGAN (the SDV-family tabular GAN models) are run unmodified as baseline data generators, with TGAN's hyperparameters tuned via its sdv-dev GitHub search tool, and both are benchmarked against the authors' proposed comfortGAN.
evidence: "The hyper-parameters tuning for TGAN [47] was done utilizing its random hyper-parameters search" citing https://sdv-dev.github.io/TGAN/readme.html#model-parameters; CTGAN [46] and TGAN [47] run as GAN-variant baselines against the authors' comfortGAN across all datasets and metrics (Table 1).
venue: BuildSys '20: 7th ACM International Conference on Systems for Energy-Efficient Built Environments

title: BatteryPass-12K: The First Dataset for the Novel Digital Battery Passport Conformance Task
summary: This paper introduces BatteryPass-12K, the first public benchmark dataset for classifying digital battery passport (DBP) conformance to EU battery regulation, created synthetically from real pilot samples, and evaluates 22 language models on the task in zero-shot and few-shot settings. The SDV paper is listed among a string of general citations on synthetic data generation in machine learning and is not engaged with further; SDV's synthetic data vault concept is only cited, not used to produce the dataset.
evidence: "Although generating synthetic DBPs is new, synthetic data generation has been a common approach in machine learning (ML)[22–28]." with [22] being the SDV DSAA 2016 paper, cited only in a list of general synthetic-data references; full text confirms no SDV-family term appears outside the reference list.

title: BayesBoost: Identifying and Handling Bias Using Synthetic Data Generators
summary: This paper presents BayesBoost, a method that uses Bayesian networks to identify hard-to-predict data samples in ground-truth healthcare datasets and boost their representation when generating synthetic data, aiming to reduce under-representation bias carried into synthetic patient data. The generative approach itself is built on Bayesian networks rather than SDV models, and experiments evaluate predictive performance on synthetic samples produced this way. The SDV paper (Patki et al., 2016) is cited only once in the introduction as an example of generative modeling for synthetic data, with no SDV component actually run.
affiliations: Medicine and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
Medicine and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
Medicine and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency
evidence: 'Synthetic data generation occurs by applying techniques such as building generative models based on real data (Patki et al., 2016).' — a single passing citation to the SDV paper with no SDV code, model, or component run in the study.

title: A Bayesian Framework for Evaluating Scenario Compatibility in Generative Population Synthesis
summary: This paper proposes an ensemble-based Bayesian updating framework to assess whether scenario-level aggregate targets imposed on generative population synthesis models are compatible with the model's learned structural support, using effective sample size to quantify posterior concentration under conditioning. A population-aware conditional variational autoencoder is developed as the core generator, and its performance is compared against classical (Bayesian network) and deep generative baselines including TVAE. TVAE, the variational-autoencoder tabular synthesizer originally introduced in the CTGAN paper, is run as one of several baseline models in the experimental comparison table.
affiliations: KTH Royal Institute of Technology; Monash University
evidence: "TVAE[15]. A variational autoencoder designed for tabular data generation..." is listed as a baseline model with results reported in Table II (SRMSE, precision/recall/F1) alongside BN, BN-Copula, and the authors' SemaPop-VAE models; no library import or package name is given.
needs: Cannot confirm from the evidence whether TVAE was run via the sdv-dev/ctgan package or reimplemented by the authors; integration marked unclear pending that detail.

title: Benchmarking Differentially Private Synthetic Data Generation Algorithms
summary: This paper presents a systematic empirical benchmark comparing differentially private synthetic tabular data generation algorithms -- GAN-based, marginal-based, and workload-based -- across multiple datasets, tasks, and privacy budgets, measuring attribute-distribution similarity, pairwise correlation, and downstream ML classification accuracy. It evaluates DP variants such as DP-CTGAN and PATE-CTGAN alongside marginal methods like MST and PrivBayes, finding GAN-based approaches often fail to beat simple baselines. SDGym, the SDV-family benchmarking harness, is explicitly run as the platform for all experiments and its metrics inspire the paper's own evaluation groups.
affiliations: Tumult Labs; University of Massachusetts Amherst
Tumult Labs; University of Massachusetts Amherst
evidence: "We use SDGym [37] as the platform for all the experiments." and "These metrics are inspired by SDGym [3]."
needs: Reference numbering appears inconsistent (SDGym cited both as [3] the GitHub repo and mislabeled [37], which in the bibliography is actually the CTGAN NeurIPS paper) -- a likely mis-citation rather than an error in our reading.

title: Benchmarking the Fidelity and Utility of Synthetic Relational Data
summary: This paper presents a benchmarking methodology and open-source tool for evaluating the fidelity and utility of synthetic relational (multi-table) data, comparing six methods including two commercial tools across several real-world relational datasets. The authors implement new fidelity metrics and utility evaluation procedures, using SDMetrics for multi-table quality assessment and the SDV metadata format for dataset specification. SDV's Gaussian-copula-based relational synthesizer is run as one of the primary methods evaluated throughout the benchmark, and SDMetrics is used and extended for quality/detection metrics.
evidence: "The foundations of synthesizing relational data were laid by the Synthetic Data Vault (Patki et al., 2016)." SDV is run as a compared method across all benchmark datasets (AirBnB, Rossmann, Walmart, Biodegradability, CORA, MovieLens), and SDMetrics is used/extended for multi-table quality evaluation.

title: Benders-Based Solution Strategies for Stochastic Capacity Expansion Models with Loss of Load Probability Constraints
summary: This preprint develops Benders-decomposition-based solution strategies for stochastic capacity expansion planning models that incorporate loss-of-load-probability (LOLP) chance constraints, targeting power system reliability and investment planning under uncertainty. No abstract or full text was available to determine how synthetic data methods factor into the modeling or experiments. The work cites the original Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper, but the evidence gives no indication that SDV's software was run rather than merely referenced.
evidence: Metadata indicates the paper cites the SDV DSAA-2016 paper ('cites_which_sdv_papers': ['sdv-dsaa-2016']); no citing sentence or abstract text was provided to show how or whether SDV software was used.

title: Beyond Internal Data: Constructing Complete Datasets for Fairness Testing
summary: This paper proposes a method for constructing complete synthetic test datasets for fairness auditing by learning the joint distribution over two separate, overlapping real datasets, allowing demographic attributes to be paired with model features when no single complete dataset is accessible. It validates the synthetic data's fidelity and shows that fairness metrics computed on it match those from real data, using Adult, COMPAS and German Credit as test domains. CTGAN is run with default hyperparameters as a baseline generator trained on the full dataset for comparison, and the TVD Complement fidelity metric from the original SDV paper is used throughout to score synthetic data quality.
evidence: "Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN) [49] is a state-of-the-art method that learns from the full dataset, unlike our method... we include its performance using default hyperparameters for comparison." TVD Complement metric ([34], the SDV paper) is used to evaluate fidelity of synthetic data.
venue: Algorithmic Fairness through the Lens of Metrics and Evaluation (AFME) at NeurIPS 2024

title: Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Neural Networks for Differentially Private Tabular Data Synthesis
summary: This paper proposes MargNet, a neural-network-based differentially private tabular data synthesizer that incorporates adaptive marginal selection (as used in statistical methods like AIM) into neural network training, aiming to outperform both statistical and neural DP synthesis baselines on densely correlated datasets. The empirical comparisons center on DP-CTGAN, a differentially private descendant of CTGAN, evaluated as one of several baseline generators. The original SDV/CTGAN paper is cited only in passing as an example of a 'strong generative model' underlying gradient-DP methods, without its architecture or code being used directly.
evidence: "For gradient-DP methods, while they are constructed on strong generative models [28], [31], DP-SGD limits the number of optimization steps..." -- CTGAN's paper is cited only generically here; the actual baseline run throughout experiments is DP-CTGAN (Fang et al. 2022), a distinct descendant work.
needs: The citation to the SDV CTGAN paper is generic and not tied to any run algorithm; the paper's extensive DP-CTGAN baseline is a separate descendant work, not SDV's CTGAN itself, so importance/integration here reflect only the passing citation.

title: Beyond Statistical Similarity: Rethinking Metrics for Deep Generative Models in Engineering Design
summary: A review and practical guide to evaluation metrics for deep generative models (VAEs, GANs, diffusion models, transformers) applied to engineering design, arguing that classic likelihood-based metrics fail to capture design-specific needs like constraint satisfaction, novelty, and conditioning. The authors curate design-specific metrics and evaluate four DGMs on bicycle frame design and topology generation problems. CTGAN's conditional GAN paper is cited only in a passing reference to prior variations of classification-accuracy-style scores, with no CTGAN model run or engaged with in the text.
evidence: CTGAN citation appears only as: "Several variations of these scores have been proposed, as in [53, 54]" where [54] is Xu et al.'s conditional GAN paper — no engagement with CTGAN itself beyond the citation.

title: BiasGuard: Guardrailing Fairness in Machine Learning Production Systems
summary: This paper proposes BiasGuard, a post-processing fairness guardrail for deployed ML systems that uses Test-Time Augmentation to generate synthetic samples with inverted protected-attribute values, then aggregates predictions on original and augmented instances to reduce bias without retraining. Experiments across legal, medical, recruitment, and census datasets show fairness gains with minimal accuracy loss, outperforming existing post-processing baselines. The entire augmentation pipeline runs on the 'Synthetic Data Vault Project' (SDV) CTGAN implementation, explicitly tuned with its embedding_dim, generator_dim, discriminator_dim, and learning-rate hyperparameters, making CTGAN's mode-specific normalization the load-bearing generative mechanism of the method.
evidence: "We used the 'Synthetic Data Vault Project' (SDV) CTGAN implementation with the following tuned hyperparameters: 500 epochs, embedding_dim set to 32, generator_dim and discriminator_dim set to (256,128,64,32), discriminator and generator learning rate set to 5e-6."

title: Black-box model risk in finance
summary: This is a discussion paper surveying the sources of risk introduced when machine learning models are used for pricing and hedging in finance, covering data risk, model risk, and mitigation strategies rather than proposing a new algorithm. In a passage on data quality remedies, the authors mention synthetic data generation tools alongside SMOTE as a way to address missing data and outlier problems. TGAN (Xu and Veeramachaneni, 2018) is cited only in passing as providing 'a convenient solution for missing data imputation and outlier treatment,' with no experiments run using it.

title: Black-Box Training Data Identification in GANs via Detector Networks
summary: This paper studies membership inference attacks against GANs in a black-box setting, where the adversary has only sample access to the generator rather than the discriminator. The authors introduce 'The Detector', a second network trained to distinguish GAN-generated samples from real ones, and evaluate it on image GANs (CIFAR10) and tabular GANs trained on genomic data. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of GANs used for tabular data generation, with no experiment run on it.

title: Boosting KNNClassifier Performance with Opposition-Based Data Transformation
summary: This preprint proposes an Opposition-Based Learning (OBL) data transformation framework that generates synthetic 'opposite' samples to augment training data, testing three OBL variants combined with K-Nearest Neighbors across 26 heterogeneous, high-dimensional datasets to improve classification performance. CTGAN is cited only in the reference list, as a specific example of generative models for tabular data, with no evidence it was implemented or run.

title: Boosting Predictive Performance on Tabular Data through Data Augmentation with Latent-Space Flow-Based Diffusion
summary: The paper proposes a family of latent-space, tree-driven diffusion methods (PCAForest, EmbedForest, AttentionForest) that couple conditional flow matching with gradient-boosted trees for minority-class oversampling on tabular data, evaluated across 11 healthcare, finance, and manufacturing datasets for utility, distributional similarity, and privacy. CTGAN, described as using mode-specific normalization and a conditional generator, is run as one of the baseline oversampling methods (alongside SMOTE and ForestDiffusion) against which the proposed methods are compared on every dataset and ratio sweep.
evidence: "benchmarks against SMOTE, CTGAN, and Forest-Diffusion using (a) downstream utility... (b) distributional similarity, and (c) empirical privacy" — CTGAN results appear in every comparison table (e.g., Table 9) across all 11 datasets.

title: Breaking Distortion-free Watermarks in Large Language Models
summary: This paper studies adversarial reverse-engineering of distortion-free LLM watermarking schemes, proposing an adaptive prompting and sorting-based algorithm to recover the hidden watermark key and mount spoofing attacks against watermarked LLMs like LLAMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct. The empirical work is entirely on LLM watermarking and text generation, unrelated to tabular data synthesis. CTGAN is cited only in the reference list, with no engagement in the body text.

title: Breaking the Quality–Privacy Tradeoff in Tabular Data Generation via In-Context Learning
summary: This paper proposes DiffICL, an in-context-learning approach to tabular data synthesis that pretrains structural priors across many datasets so that generation from a small target dataset infers a distribution rather than memorizing training samples, improving the quality-privacy tradeoff and downstream data augmentation on 14 real-world datasets. CTGAN and TVAE (both introduced in the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper) are run as baseline generators across all benchmark tables, and the paper's distributional-similarity metrics (Shape and Trend) are drawn from the SDV/SDMetrics quality-report framework. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE synthesizers are run as comparison baselines throughout the empirical evaluation, and the SDV-derived Shape/Trend quality metrics are used to score generated data.
evidence: "we evaluate representative methods from different paradigms—tabDDPM [18], TVAE [43], and CTGAN [43]—on the Adult [17] dataset"; also "For distributional similarity metrics... (1) Shape [31] measures column-wise similarity... (2) Trend [31] evaluates pairwise correlation between columns"

title: BSTabDiff: Block-Subunit Diffusion Priors for High-Dimensional Tabular Data Generation
summary: This paper proposes BSTabDiff, a block-subunit generative framework for tabular data in the High-Dimensional Low-Sample-Size (HDLSS) regime, such as omics data, that partitions features into latent blocks and models each block with a Gaussian-copula-driven decoder plus a diffusion or flow prior on block latents. It is evaluated against several baseline generators on eight HDLSS datasets using downstream TSTR/TRTR classification utility. CTGAN and its VAE counterpart TVAE (from the SDV-family CTGAN paper) are run as GAN- and VAE-based baseline generators in the empirical comparison, while an SDV system-based synthesizer (Patki et al., 2016) is cited only in passing as prior tabular-synthesis work.

title: BuddyBench: A Privacy-Constrained Multi-Task Benchmark for Pediatric Social-Communication Personalization
summary: BuddyBench is a benchmark linking drill-level learning trajectories, standardized clinical assessments, self-report data, and randomized-treatment endpoints from two pediatric autism/social-communication intervention cohorts, supporting knowledge tracing, next-drill recommendation, clinical prediction, and causal inference tasks. The paper also releases BuddyBench-Sim, a synthetic companion dataset intended to allow reproducible evaluation while protecting real clinical records, paired with membership-inference privacy audits. SDV and CTGAN are cited alongside TabDDPM as existing tabular data generation methods that motivate the paper's synthetic-data-plus-privacy-audit approach, but no experimental detail ties BuddyBench-Sim's generation specifically to the SDV library or CTGAN model.

title: CALEB: A Conditional Adversarial Learning Framework to Enhance Bot Detection
summary: This paper proposes CALEB, a framework using Conditional GAN and Auxiliary Classifier GAN to simulate evolving social bot behavior and generate synthetic bot instances that augment training data for more adaptive bot detection on Twitter. The authors evaluate the fidelity of their synthetic data against real data and against ADASYN-generated data using two statistical similarity metrics. These metrics, the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test and continuous KL Divergence, are drawn from the Synthetic Data Vault's evaluation toolkit and run directly to score how closely the generated bot instances match the original distributions.
evidence: "we present the similarity between the original data and different sets of synthetic data (CGAN, AC-GAN, and ADASYN), using two synthetic data evaluation metrics from the Synthetic Data Vault [44], the Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS) test and the continuous Kullback-Leibler (KL) Divergence metric."

title: Can You Rely on Your Model Evaluation? Improving Model Evaluation with Synthetic Test Data
summary: This NeurIPS 2023 paper introduces 3S Testing, a deep generative modeling framework that produces synthetic test sets to improve evaluation of ML models on underrepresented subgroups and under simulated distributional shifts, showing it outperforms real-test-data baselines in estimating minority-subgroup performance. The framework's main experiments rely on CTGAN as the underlying generative model, chosen for its conditional generation of subgroup- or shift-specific data, and it is also compared against TVAE and normalizing flows as alternative base generators. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run as the core generator throughout the paper's empirical programme, leveraging its conditional sampling mechanism for subgroup and shift simulation.

title: CaPS: Collaborative and Private Synthetic Data Generation from Distributed Sources
summary: This paper proposes CaPS, a framework for collaboratively generating differentially private synthetic tabular data from distributed data holders, replacing the trusted aggregator with secure multi-party computation (MPC) protocols and combining this with differential privacy for output privacy. It demonstrates scalability and applicability for state-of-the-art marginal-based select-measure-generate algorithms MWEM+PGM and AIM. title: CasualSynth: Generating Structurally Sound Synthetic Data
summary: This paper proposes CausalSynth, a framework that decouples causal structure generation (via structural causal models and ancestral sampling) from semantic realization (via an LLM 'realizer'), with an iterative consistency-verification loop to correct violations of imposed causal structure. It is evaluated on three causal benchmarks (ASIA, ALARM, MIMIC-Struct) against LLM prompting, latent-variable generators, diffusion-based tabular generators, and causal-discovery baselines. CTGAN is one of the latent-variable baselines run for comparison against the proposed framework.
